instructions.name: DS_BPERMUTE_B32
instructions.description: Backward permute. This does not access LDS memory and may be called even if no LDS memory is allocated to the wave. It uses LDS hardware to implement an arbitrary swizzle across threads in a wavefront.

instructions.name: DS_BVH_STACK_RTN_B32
instructions.description: Ray tracing involves traversing a BVH which is a kind of tree where nodes have up to 4 children. Each shader thread processes one child at a time, and overflow nodes are stored temporarily in LDS using a stack. This instruction supports pushing/popping the stack to reduce the number of VALU instructions required per traversal and reduce VMEM bandwidth requirements.

fields.name: ABS
fields.description: If ABS[N] set, take the floating-point absolute value of the N'th input operand. This is applied before negation. See OPF_NOABS for instructions that do not allow this input modifier.

fields.name: CLAMP
fields.description: If set, clamp or signal on output. VCMP instructions enable signaling-compare. For floating point outputs, clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. For signed integer outputs, clamp to [MIN_INT, MAX_INT]. For unsigned integer outputs, clamp to [0, MAX_UINT]. Applied after output modifier. See OPF_NOCLAMP for a list of instructions that do not support clamping or signaling.

fields.name: NEG
fields.description: If NEG[N] set, take the floating-point negation of the N'th input operand. This is applied after absolute value. See OPF_NONEG for a list of instructions that do not support negation.

fields.name: OMOD
fields.description:
Output modifier for instruction. Only useful for floating point outputs; integer outputs should set this to OMOD_OFF. Applied before clamping. See OPF_NOOMOD for a list of instructions that do not support output modifier.

Output modifiers apply to single and double floating point results only. Integer and packed float 16 results ignore the omod setting.

Output modifiers are not compatible with output denorms. If output denorms are allowed, then any output modifier is ignored. If output denorms are not allowed, then denorms are flushed to +/-0 and the output modifier is applied. If modifier is non-zero, -0 is forced to +0. If an instruction forces output denorm to be disabled then the output modifier can be applied on the result no matter the output denorm setting.

Output modifiers are not IEEE compliant (-0*x=+0). Output modifiers are ignored by hardware if ieee mode is set.

fields.name: OP_SEL

fields.name: DMASK
fields.description:
Enable mask for image read/write data components. Normally bit 0 is red, 1 is green, 2 is blue and 3 is alpha. At least 1 bit must be on. Data is assumed to be packed into consecutive VGPRs.

For reads, defines which components are returned.

For writes, defines which components are written with data from VGPRs (missing components get 0).

Enabled components come from consecutive VGPRs. For example when DMASK = 'b1001 the red component is in VDATA0 and the alpha component is in VDATA1.

For D16 reads, DMASK indicates which components to return.

For D16 writes, the DMASK indicates which components to write but has restrictions: Data is read out of consecutive VGPRs: LSBs of VDATA, then MSBs of VDATA, then LSBs of VDATA+1 and last if needed MSBs of VDATA+1. This is regardless of which DMASK bits are set, only how many bits are set. The position of the DMASK bits controls which components are written in memory.

If DMASK==0, the TA overrides with DMASK = 1 and puts zeros in VGPR followed by LWE status if exists. TFE status is not generated since the fetch is dropped.

For IMAGE_GATHER4* instructions, DMASK indicates which component (RGBA), and the number of VGPRs to use is determined automatically by hardware (4 VGPRs when D16=0, and 2 VGPRs when D16=1).

0: for image ops with samplers, (S,T,R) coordinates in [0.0, 1.0] span the entire texture map.

1: for image ops with samplers, (S,T,R) coordinates in [0.0, N] span the texture map where N is (width,height,depth).

Array index, cube slice, LOD, bias etc. are not affected. Image ops without a sampler are not affected. UINT inputs are unnormalized. This bit is logically OR'd with the SAMP.FORCE_UNNORMALIZED when sent to the texture unit.

fields.name: DMASK
fields.description:
Enable mask for image read/write data components. Normally bit 0 is red, 1 is green, 2 is blue and 3 is alpha. At least 1 bit must be on. Data is assumed to be packed into consecutive VGPRs.

For reads, defines which components are returned.

For writes, defines which components are written with data from VGPRs (missing components get 0).

Enabled components come from consecutive VGPRs. For example when DMASK = 'b1001 the red component is in VDATA0 and the alpha component is in VDATA1.

For D16 reads, DMASK indicates which components to return.

For D16 writes, the DMASK indicates which components to write but has restrictions: Data is read out of consecutive VGPRs: LSBs of VDATA, then MSBs of VDATA, then LSBs of VDATA+1 and last if needed MSBs of VDATA+1. This is regardless of which DMASK bits are set, only how many bits are set. The position of the DMASK bits controls which components are written in memory.

If DMASK==0, the TA overrides with DMASK = 1 and puts zeros in VGPR followed by LWE status if exists. TFE status is not generated since the fetch is dropped.

For IMAGE_GATHER4* instructions, DMASK indicates which component (RGBA), and the number of VGPRs to use is determined automatically by hardware (4 VGPRs when D16=0, and 2 VGPRs when D16=1).

fields.name: GLC

fields.name: LWE

fields.name: NSA

fields.name: R128
fields.description: Texture resource size: 1 = 128 bit (4 SGPRs), 0 = 256 bit (8 SGPRs).

fields.name: SSAMP

fields.name: TFE
fields.description: Texture Fail Enable (for partially resident textures).

fields.name: UNORM
fields.description:
Force address to be un-normalized regardless of texture sampler setting. Must be set to 1 for image store and atomic operations.

0: for image ops with samplers, (S,T,R) coordinates in [0.0, 1.0] span the entire texture map.

1: for image ops with samplers, (S,T,R) coordinates in [0.0, N] span the texture map where N is (width,height,depth).

Array index, cube slice, LOD, bias etc. are not affected. Image ops without a sampler are not affected. UINT inputs are unnormalized. This bit is logically OR'd with the SAMP.FORCE_UNNORMALIZED when sent to the texture unit.

fields.name: OMOD
fields.description:
Output modifier for instruction. Only useful for floating point outputs; integer outputs should set this to OMOD_OFF. Applied before clamping. See OPF_NOOMOD for a list of instructions that do not support output modifier.

Output modifiers apply to single and double floating point results only. Integer and packed float 16 results ignore the omod setting.

Output modifiers are not compatible with output denorms. If output denorms are allowed, then any output modifier is ignored. If output denorms are not allowed, then denorms are flushed to +/-0 and the output modifier is applied. If modifier is non-zero, -0 is forced to +0. If an instruction forces output denorm to be disabled then the output modifier can be applied on the result no matter the output denorm setting.

Output modifiers are not IEEE compliant (-0*x=+0). Output modifiers are ignored by hardware if ieee mode is set.

fields.name: CLAMP
fields.description: If set, clamp or signal on output. VCMP instructions enable signaling-compare. For floating point outputs, clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. For signed integer outputs, clamp to [MIN_INT, MAX_INT]. For unsigned integer outputs, clamp to [0, MAX_UINT]. Applied after output modifier. See OPF_NOCLAMP for a list of instructions that do not support clamping or signaling.

fields.name: NEG_HI

fields.name: OP_SEL
fields.description: OP_SEL[N] determines if lower [15:0] or upper [31:16] bits are selected for the N'th source for the LOW OPERATION. 0 selects the lower order bits and 1 selects the higher order bits.

fields.name: OP_SEL_HI
